documents.name: price-list.txt
documents.text:
Harbor Lane Freight price list (invented).
Starter plan: 18 dollars per seat per month, up to 10 seats, no single sign-on.
Professional plan: 52 dollars per seat per month, billed yearly, includes single sign-on and live re-routing.
Enterprise plan: custom price, from 200 seats, includes a dedicated support manager.
Onboarding: a one-time fee of 1,500 dollars for any plan, covering setup and two training days.
Discounts: at most 10 percent, only for a yearly plan paid upfront, and only with approval from the sales director.
Contract: yearly, renews automatically; cancellation needs 30 days written notice before the renewal date.

tail.text: BEFORE WE GO ON WHAT IS ACTUALLY THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN SAML AND OPEN ID CONNECT

question: BEFORE WE GO ON WHAT IS ACTUALLY THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN SAML AND OPEN ID CONNECT
mustInclude: a direct answer to the difference, from general knowledge, stated with confidence
SAML passes signed XML assertions, usually through the browser, and is the older standard common in enterprise web apps
OpenID Connect is an identity layer on top of OAuth 2.0 that uses JSON web tokens and suits modern web and mobile apps
mustNotInclude: a promise to confirm, check or follow up after the call
hedging such as "I think", "I believe", "I'm not sure" or "roughly speaking"
any claim about which one Harbor Lane supports, since the documents only say single sign-on is included
